1	/**
     2	 * Workspace Detail View — Repo Parallelizer GUI.
     3	 *
     4	 * Renders the full detail page for a single workspace inside a project:
     5	 *   - Workspace header: ID, description, breadcrumb link back to the project.
     6	 *   - Repository status table: one row per repository, showing current branch,
     7	 *     a color-coded Git status badge, an error/loading indicator for repos
     8	 *     with no status data yet, and an Actions column containing an "Open"
     9	 *     button that opens the repository in GitHub Desktop via
    10	 *     `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop(projectId, wid, repoId)`.
    11	 *   - Live polling: status badges refresh in-place via a 1-second countdown
    12	 *     interval that triggers a poll every 10 seconds. A visible countdown
    13	 *     label and a "Refresh Now" button provide user control. The interval
    14	 *     is cleared via the cleanup function returned from
    15	 *     `renderWorkspaceDetail`, which the router calls before navigating
    16	 *     away.
    17	 *   - Actions: "Open in VS Code" button (shown only when workspace is
    18	 *     initialised, dynamically added after a successful Setup — calls
    19	 *     `api.workspaces.launch.vscode`), "Switch Branches" navigation button,
    20	 *     "Rename Workspace" (disabled for STABLE), "Delete Workspace" (disabled
    21	 *     for STABLE).
    22	 *
    23	 * ## Credential-error display
    24	 *
    25	 * When a repository's clone fails because no credential is configured for its
    26	 * host, the setup orchestrators emit an error message containing the sentinel
    27	 * text defined by `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` ("requires a credential for
    28	 * host"). The view detects this via `applySetupResultCredentialErrors()` and
    29	 * replaces the generic "No data" badge in the status table with an amber
    30	 * "Missing Credential" badge (`.status-badge-credential`) that links directly
    31	 * to `#/repositories/:id` so the user can assign a credential without leaving
    32	 * the workflow.
    33	 *
    34	 * Key helpers in this subsystem:
    35	 *   - `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` — the exact string matched against error
    36	 *     messages. Defined in `gui/public/js/utils/constants.js`; imported here.
    37	 *     Must stay in sync with the orchestrator error templates.
    38	 *   - `buildMissingCredentialBadge(repoId)` — renders the amber `<a>` badge
    39	 *     and wires SPA navigation via `_router` (with `href` as a fallback).
    40	 *   - `applySetupResultCredentialErrors(setupResult)` — called after every
    41	 *     setup invocation (Setup button, Retry Setup, health alert) to add or
    42	 *     remove repos from the in-memory `credentialErrorRepoIds` Set and update
    43	 *     their badge cell in the DOM immediately.
    44	 *   - `applyStatusMapUpdate()` — clears the credential-error flag when a repo
    45	 *     transitions from no-data to having live status data (i.e. after a
    46	 *     successful re-clone following credential assignment).
    47	 *
    48	 * **Known limitation:** `credentialErrorRepoIds` is an in-memory Set populated
    49	 * only by explicit `setup()` calls during the current page session. If the page
    50	 * is reloaded after a prior credential-missing failure, the badge will not
    51	 * appear until the next Setup run because the error state is not persisted in
    52	 * the workspace health report or the status map. Surfacing this on page load
    53	 * would require a new API endpoint or server-side persistence — out of scope
    54	 * for the current implementation.
    55	 *
    56	 * ## Router integration
    57	 *
    58	 * The view uses the same router-injection pattern as `project-detail.js`:
    59	 * `app.js` calls `setRouter(router)` before `router.start()`. The `_router`
    60	 * variable is null-guarded at every navigation site so the view remains
    61	 * functional in test contexts.
    62	 *
    63	 * ## Cleanup contract
    64	 *
    65	 * `renderWorkspaceDetail` returns a cleanup function. The router's `_render`
    66	 * method already stores and calls any function returned by a view. No changes
    67	 * to `router.js` are needed.
    68	 *
    69	 * @module workspace-detail
    70	 */
    71	
    72	import { api }               from '../api.js';
    73	import { showToast }         from '../components/toast.js';
    74	import { showConfirm }       from '../components/confirm-dialog.js';
    75	import { buildRepoStatusCells, makeBranchTrigger, updateRepoStatusCells } from '../components/repo-status-cells.js';
    76	import { createFormField, validateRequired, WORKSPACE_ID_PATTERN } from '../components/form-helpers.js';

    78	import { STABLE_WS_ID, APP_NAME_SHORT, CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL } from '../utils/constants.js';

1	# GUI Frontend
     2	
     3	The frontend is a vanilla JavaScript SPA with no build step, served as static files by the built-in HTTP server from `gui/public/`.
     4	
     5	## Architecture
     6	
     7	- **Routing:** Hash-based client-side router (`#/path`) with named parameter extraction (`:id`, `:wid`).
     8	- **Module system:** Native ES modules loaded by the browser. No bundler.
     9	- **State management:** None — every view fetches fresh data from the REST API on render. Mutations trigger a full view re-render.
    10	- **Styling:** Pico CSS (classless variant) as base layer, with a custom `styles.css` override layer using CSS custom properties. Light/dark theme switching via `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`.
    11	
    12	## Router
    13	
    14	The `Router` class (`gui/public/js/router.js`) manages view lifecycle:
    15	
    16	1. Listens for `hashchange` events.
    17	2. Matches the hash against registered patterns.
    18	3. Calls the previous view's cleanup function (if returned).
    19	4. Clears the `#app` container.
    20	5. Calls the matched view function with `(container, params)`.
    21	6. Stores any cleanup function returned by the view.
    22	
    23	## Routes
    24	
    25	| Hash Pattern | View | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `#/` | `dashboard.js` | Project listing with a filter/sort toolbar and a "Create Project" form. The toolbar (`.project-filter-toolbar`) sits between the page header and the project list and contains three labelled controls — each has a visible `<label class="filter-label">` with a `for`/`id` binding: a debounced search input (`id="project-filter-search"`, `type="search"`, ~250 ms), a repository filter `<select id="project-filter-repo">` populated from `api.repositories.list()` (always rendered; disabled with a "No repositories" placeholder when no repos exist or when the fetch fails — a toast is shown on failure), and a sort `<select id="project-filter-sort">` with `alpha` (Alphabetical, default) and `activity` (Last Activity) options. All three controls fire an `onFilterChange(FilterState)` callback on change. The current filter state (`{ search, repoId, sort }`) is maintained in `renderDashboard` and flows into `buildFilterToolbar`, `applyFiltersAndSort`, and `renderProjectGrid`. `applyFiltersAndSort(filterState, allProjects)` is a pure exported function — it receives the project list as an explicit parameter (no closure over module state) and can be unit-tested without DOM involvement. Filter changes re-apply the current state to the in-memory `_allProjects` cache without re-fetching; creating a new project re-fetches all project data from the API and re-applies the current filter/sort state. An empty-state message — "No projects match the current filters." vs "No projects yet." — distinguishes filtered-empty from truly-empty lists. |
    28	| `#/repositories` | `repositories.js` | Repository CRUD table. Each row's **Name** column renders as a clickable `<a class="repo-name-display repo-name-link">` element linking to `#/repositories/${encodeURIComponent(repo.id)}`. Clicking Edit switches the Name cell to an inline `<input>` for in-place editing; Save/Cancel restore the link with updated or original text. A **Credential** column shows a CSS-styled badge built by `buildCredentialBadge()` from `utils/dom.js`: `.credential-badge.credential-badge--set` (green checkmark, `aria-label="Credential configured"`) when a credential is associated, or `.credential-badge.credential-badge--none` (muted dash, `aria-label="No credential configured"`) when none is set. |
    29	| `#/repositories/:id` | `repository-detail.js` | Repository overview: a **Credential** section followed by a table of every workspace across every project that contains the given repository. The Credential section (built by `buildCredentialSection(repoId, storedCredentialId)`) fetches `GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options` asynchronously and renders a `<select>` dropdown with a "None" option plus each matching credential as `label (host)`. When exactly one credential matches and has `auto=true`, it is pre-selected with an "(auto)" suffix — multiple auto-match options intentionally leave the selection on None. When a stored `credentialId` exists it is pre-selected. Changes call `PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential` to persist the selection. The workspace table rows show Project (link to `#/projects/:pid`), Workspace (link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`), and the shared Branch/Status/Actions cells from `buildRepoStatusCells`. STABLE workspace rows show plain-text branch names; all other rows have a clickable branch-switch trigger. A "Refresh" button re-discovers the full project/workspace set (calls `api.projects.list()` + the full fan-out) and diffs against the existing rows: new rows are appended, removed rows are dropped, and existing rows are updated in-place via `api.status.refresh()` — protected by a `refreshInProgress` mutex. A 404 response for the repository renders a "not found" message with a link back to `#/repositories`. An empty-state message is shown when no projects contain the repository. Individual project/workspace fetch failures are handled gracefully via `Promise.allSettled` — partial results are displayed and a warning toast is shown when any fetch failed. The webserver URL is fetched once during initial load; the "Browse" button is shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback (`(msg) => showToast(msg, 'error')`) so Git GUI button failures are surfaced as toasts without a dynamic `import('./toast.js')` inside the component. |
    30	| `#/projects/:id` | `project-detail.js` | Project metadata, tabbed repo/workspace/danger-zone management. The workspace table includes a **Health** column: initialized workspaces with health issues show a warning badge with issue count; healthy and uninitialized workspaces show an empty cell. Health is fetched in parallel with status for all initialized workspaces via `Promise.allSettled` (graceful degradation — fetch failures leave the health cell empty). The project's repository table (`buildRepositoriesSection`) includes a **Credential** column built by `buildCredentialBadge()` from `utils/dom.js`: `.credential-badge.credential-badge--set` when a credential is associated, `.credential-badge.credential-badge--none` when none is set. |
    31	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | `workspace-detail.js` | Live git status with countdown-based polling and manual refresh. Health report fetched in parallel on initial load and on every poll/refresh cycle. Unhealthy workspaces render a `.health-alert` card with per-issue rows and fix buttons (`Regenerate File` for `regenerate-workspace-file` issues, `Fix Setup` for `setup-workspace` issues). The header management row includes an **"Open in VS Code"** button (shown only when `workspace.initialized` is `true`; dynamically inserted after a successful Setup without a full re-render). The repository status table has a 4th **"Actions"** column; each repository row contains a **"Browse"** button (shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured, opens `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/` in a new tab via `window.open`) followed by a **"Git GUI"** button that calls `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop()`. The webserver URL is fetched once during the initial data load (in parallel with other requests) via `api.config.webserverUrl.get()`. In non-STABLE workspaces, each **Branch** cell is a clickable trigger (`<button class="branch-switch-trigger">`) that opens an inline quick-switch popover via `showBranchQuickSwitch()`. STABLE workspace branch cells remain plain text. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback so Git GUI button failures show as toasts. DOM clearing uses `clearElement()` from `utils/dom.js` throughout (no `innerHTML = ''` assignments). A **Notes** section (built by `buildNotesSection()`) is appended below the repository status table: it contains a `<textarea id="workspace-notes-textarea">` pre-populated from `workspace.notes`, a 1000 ms debounced `input` listener that calls `api.workspaces.update()`, and an `aria-live="polite"` status span that shows "Saving…" / "Saved" / "Save failed." feedback. |
    32	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch` | `branch-switch.js` | 3-step branch switch wizard. |
    33	| `#/settings` | `settings.js` | Settings view with four sections: **Git Credentials** (add, inline-edit, and delete named per-host PATs; each credential has a Label, Host, and Token; the credentials table renders columns Label / Host / Token / Actions; clicking Edit enables inline editing of Label and Token — Host is read-only; clicking Save calls `PUT /api/config/credentials` with the credential id; clicking Delete calls `DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id` with a confirmation dialog that warns about affected repositories), **Repositories Refresh Delay** (configurable `gitPollingIntervalSeconds`), **Webserver URL** (base URL of the local webserver; enables the "Browse" button in the workspace-detail view), and **Notes Display** (card height in px and column count for the notes grid, backed by `GET/PUT /api/config/notes-display`). All non-credentials sections share a single **"Save Settings"** footer button that calls each section's `save()` function in parallel via `Promise.all()`. The Notes Display section is built by `buildNotesDisplaySection()`, which uses CSS classes `notes-display-section` (section wrapper), `notes-display-input-row` (flex row for label + input + unit), `notes-display-label` (label element), `notes-display-input` (number input), and `notes-display-unit` (unit span, e.g. "px"). |
    34	| `#/error-log` | `error-log.js` | Paginated, filterable error log table with expandable detail rows and "Clear All" action. |
    35	| `#/notes` | `notes-collected.js` | Two-panel notes view: a left sidebar listing all workspaces grouped by collapsible project groups (workspaces with notes carry a `.has-notes` class and a blue dot indicator), and a right scrollable main panel of editable note cards. On initial load only workspaces with non-empty notes show cards. Clicking a sidebar item for a workspace with a card scrolls the main panel to it; clicking one without a card creates a new empty card and focuses the textarea. Each card header contains a clickable workspace ID link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`. Textareas auto-save after 1000 ms of inactivity via `api.workspaces.update()`; saving empty text removes the card and clears the sidebar indicator. A `.notes-empty-state` message is shown when no cards are present. |
    36	
    37	> **Maintainer note — Settings sections:** `settings.js` has a module-level JSDoc block (at the top of the file) that lists all active settings sections. When adding or removing a `build*Section()` factory from `settings.js`, update that JSDoc list to keep it in sync with the route description in this table.
    38	
    39	## API Client
    40	
    41	`api.js` exports a namespaced `api` object with eight top-level groups:
    42	
    43	- `api.repositories` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `delete(id)`, `touchRefreshTimestamp(id)`, `credentialOptions(id)`, `updateCredential(id, credentialId)`
    44	- `api.projects` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `rename(id, newId)`, `delete(id)`, `addRepository(pid, rid)`, `removeRepository(pid, rid)`
    45	- `api.workspaces` — `list(pid)`, `get(pid, wid)`, `create(pid, data)`, `update(pid, wid, data)`, `rename(pid, wid, newId)`, `delete(pid, wid)`, `setup(pid, wid)`, `health(pid, wid)`, `regenerateFile(pid, wid)`, `launch.vscode(pid, wid)`, `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)`
    46	- `api.branches` — `list(pid, wid)`, `switch(pid, wid, assignments)`
    47	- `api.status` — `get(pid, wid)`, `refresh(pid, wid)`
    48	- `api.config.credentials` — `list()`, `add(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `remove(id)`
    49	- `api.config.polling` — `get()`, `set(seconds)`
    50	- `api.config.webserverUrl` — `get()`, `set(url)`
    51	- `api.config.notesDisplay` — `get()`, `set(data)`
    52	- `api.errorLog` — `list(params?)`, `get(id)`, `clear()`, `count()`
    53	- `api.notes` — `list()`
    54	
    55	### `api.repositories` — Credential Methods
    56	
    57	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| `credentialOptions(id)` | `GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options` | Fetch credentials compatible with the repository's URL hostname. Returns an array of `{ credentialId, label, host, auto }` objects. An empty array is returned when no credentials match or the URL is non-HTTPS (e.g. SSH). |
    60	| `updateCredential(id, credentialId)` | `PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential` | Associate a credential with the repository, or clear the association. Pass `''` (empty string) to clear. Returns the updated repository object. |
    61	
    62	**`updateCredential` caller contract:** `credentialId` must always be a `string`. Passing `undefined` causes `JSON.stringify` to silently strip the key from the request body, producing an empty `{}` payload instead of `{ credentialId: '' }`. Always pass `''` when the intent is to clear the association.
    63	
    64	**`credentialOptions` auto-select semantics:** Each returned option includes an `auto` boolean. The GUI pre-selects an option only when exactly one option is returned with `auto: true`. When multiple options share `auto: true` (multiple credentials for the same host), none is pre-selected — the user must choose explicitly.
    65	
    66	---
    67	
    68	### `api.workspaces` — Health & File Methods
    69	
    70	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    71	|---|---|---|
    72	| `health(pid, wid)` | `GET /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/health` | Fetch the health report for an initialized workspace. Returns `{ healthy: boolean, issues: Array<{ type: string, severity: string, message: string, fixAction: string, repositoryId?: string }> }`. |
    73	| `regenerateFile(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/regenerate-workspace-file` | Regenerate the `.code-workspace` file from the current repository list without cloning. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. |
    74	
    75	**`health()` issue `fixAction` values:**
    76	- `regenerate-workspace-file` — missing or stale `.code-workspace` file; surface a `Regenerate File` button.
    77	- `setup-workspace` — uncloned repository; surface a `Fix Setup` button.
    78	
    79	### `api.workspaces.launch` — External-App Launch Methods
    80	
    81	External-application launchers are grouped under the `api.workspaces.launch` sub-namespace. New launcher methods (e.g. "Open in Terminal") should be added here rather than as flat methods on `api.workspaces`.
    82	
    83	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    84	|---|---|---|
    85	| `launch.vscode(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` | Open the workspace's `.code-workspace` file in VS Code. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the workspace file does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-vscode'`). |
    86	| `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` | Open a repository's local clone directory in GitHub Desktop. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the repository directory does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-github-desktop'`). |
    87	
    88	**Caller contract:** All path parameters (`pid`, `wid`, `rid`) are passed through `encodeURIComponent` inside `api.js`. Callers are responsible for validating that these values are not `undefined`/`null` before invoking these methods — `encodeURIComponent` will coerce them to the strings `'undefined'`/`'null'` rather than throwing.
    89	
    90	### `api.errorLog` Reference
    91	
    92	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    93	|---|---|---|
    94	| `list(params?)` | `GET /api/error-log[?...]` | Fetch error log entries with optional filtering and pagination. |
    95	| `get(id)` | `GET /api/error-log/:id` | Fetch a single entry by numeric ID. |
    96	| `clear()` | `DELETE /api/error-log` | Delete all entries. Resolves with `undefined` on HTTP 204. |
    97	| `count()` | `GET /api/error-log?limit=0` | Fetch only the total count (no entries payload). Useful for badges. |
    98	
    99	**`list()` params shape:**

100	
   101	```js
   102	api.errorLog.list({
   103	    severity: 'error',   // optional — 'error' | 'warning'
   104	    source:   'clone',   // optional — exact-match on Source field
   105	    limit:    10,        // optional — max entries to return (default 100 server-side)
   106	    offset:   0,         // optional — zero-based page offset
   107	})
   108	```
   109	
   110	All params are optional. Omitting `params` entirely (or passing `undefined`) sends a bare `GET /api/error-log`.
   111	
   112	**`clear()` 204 contract:** The underlying `request()` helper resolves with `undefined` when the server returns HTTP 204 (no body). Callers should not try to read a response value from `clear()`.
   113	
   114	**`count()` pattern:** Sends `GET /api/error-log?limit=0`. The server returns `{ entries: [], total: N }`. Read `response.total` for the count. This is the recommended approach for polling a badge counter without transferring entry data.

   136	
   137	### Repo Status Cells Component
   138	
   139	`components/repo-status-cells.js` encapsulates the reusable Branch, Status badge, and Actions cell-building logic shared between the workspace-detail and repository-detail views. It exports three named functions:
   140	
   141	#### `buildRepoStatusCells(opts)`
   142	
   143	Builds the three shared status `<td>` cells for a single repository row.
   144	
   145	| Option | Type | Required | Description |
   146	|---|---|---|---|
   147	| `repoId` | `string` | Yes | Unique repository identifier. |
   148	| `repoName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable display name; used in aria-labels. Falls back to `repoId` when no richer name is available. |
   149	| `statusInfo` | `Object\|null` | Yes | `GitStatusInfo` from the API, or `null` when no status data is available yet. |

    18	 *     initialised, dynamically added after a successful Setup — calls

    22	 *
    23	 * ## Credential-error display
    24	 *
    25	 * When a repository's clone fails because no credential is configured for its
    26	 * host, the setup orchestrators emit an error message containing the sentinel
    27	 * text defined by `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` ("requires a credential for
    28	 * host"). The view detects this via `applySetupResultCredentialErrors()` and
    29	 * replaces the generic "No data" badge in the status table with an amber
    30	 * "Missing Credential" badge (`.status-badge-credential`) that links directly
    31	 * to `#/repositories/:id` so the user can assign a credential without leaving
    32	 * the workflow.
    33	 *
    34	 * Key helpers in this subsystem:
    35	 *   - `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` — the exact string matched against error
    36	 *     messages. Defined in `gui/public/js/utils/constants.js`; imported here.
    37	 *     Must stay in sync with the orchestrator error templates.
    38	 *   - `buildMissingCredentialBadge(repoId)` — renders the amber `<a>` badge
    39	 *     (`.status-badge-credential`) and wires SPA navigation via `_router`
    40	 *     (with `href` as a fallback). **Distinct from `buildCredentialBadge()`
    41	 *     in `utils/dom.js`:** this badge is an `<a>` element that signals a
    42	 *     *clone failure* in the workspace status table and links to the
    43	 *     repository settings page; `buildCredentialBadge()` is a `<span>` that
    44	 *     shows the *assignment status* of a credential in the repository list
    45	 *     (`.credential-badge--set` / `.credential-badge--none`). The two badges
    46	 *     serve different views and must not be conflated.
    47	 *   - `applySetupResultCredentialErrors(setupResult)` — called after every
